blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Running security policies effectively means treating the policy as a living tool, not a legal document that sits in a drawer. A policy that nobody reads is worse than no policy at all, because it gives a false sense of protection.

The good intermediate approach has three habits. First, write the policy in plain language that a non-technical employee can actually read in five minutes. Second, teach it with real examples, not abstract rules. Third, measure it: how many employees have completed the short training? How many reported an incident this quarter? How many recognised a test phishing email?

We are running a short, quarterly refresh — not long training sessions. Every refresh takes three minutes. Employees pay attention because it is short, and the policy stays alive because the refresh never stops.

items.q: According to the text, why is a policy that nobody reads worse than no policy at all?
options: It gives a false sense of protection
It is too long to print
items.why: "it gives a false sense of protection" — as pessoas acham que estão seguras quando não estão.

items.q: Which three habits define the good intermediate approach?
options: Legal review, long training, annual audits
Plain language, real examples, measured outcomes
items.why: "write the policy in plain language… teach it with real examples… measure it".

items.q: How long does each quarterly refresh take?
items.why: "Every refresh takes three minutes."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A detailed 40-page policy locked in a drawer is the safest option
Real examples teach better than abstract rules
A short, frequent refresh keeps the policy alive
items.why: Inferência: o texto todo defende o oposto — um documento que ninguém lê é pior que nada.

items.q: The emphasis on measuring incidents and phishing tests suggests that the author believes…
options: a policy should prove it changes behaviour, not just exist
security is only the IT team's job
employees should be punished for mistakes
training should be judged by attendance alone
items.why: Inferência: medir resultados (incidentes, phishing) mostra que o objetivo é comportamento real, não papel.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte apresentando a mudança da política de segurança à equipe. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Good morning, everyone. Right now I'm holding the old security policy — forty pages, and honestly, almost nobody reads it. That's the problem I'm here to fix.

From this quarter, we're replacing it with a three-minute refresh. It's short, it's plain, and it goes out every three months. No more all-day sessions, no more dense legal language. If a policy sits in a drawer, it protects no one — it just makes us feel safe.

Now, here is something that surprised a few managers. Since we launched the first refresh, incident reports are going up, not down. That's good news. People are finally recognising a suspicious email and telling us about it. Before, they stayed quiet because they didn't know what to look for.

So when you see that number rising this quarter, don't panic. We are not less secure — we are more aware. I'm tracking two things: how many of you finish the refresh, and how many spot our test phishing emails. Those numbers tell me the policy is actually alive.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is Charlotte replacing the 40-page policy with?
items.why: "we're replacing it with a three-minute refresh… every three months."

items.q: According to Charlotte, what is happening to incident reports since the first refresh?
items.why: "incident reports are going up, not down."

items.q: Why does Charlotte call the rise in incident reports good news?
options: It means the company can charge more
It means the policy can be deleted
It means people now recognise and report suspicious emails
It means fewer employees are working
items.why: "People are finally recognising a suspicious email and telling us about it."

items.q: What does Charlotte imply was the reason employees stayed quiet before?
options: They were afraid of being fired
They did not care about security
They did not know what to look for
items.why: Inferência: "they stayed quiet because they didn't know what to look for."

items.q: Charlotte's overall message about the rising numbers is best summarised as…
options: the company is now less secure and should worry
only IT should read security reports
the refresh has failed and must be cancelled
more awareness, not less security, is behind the higher numbers
items.why: Inferência: "We are not less secure — we are more aware."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We treat the policy as a living tool, updated whenever the threats change." A living tool is…
options: a legal file kept for compliance only
a document that is regularly used and updated
items.why: Living tool = ferramenta viva: algo usado e atualizado, não guardado.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "If the policy just sits in a ___, no one benefits from it."
items.why: Drawer = gaveta: a imagem de um documento esquecido e sem uso.

items.q: "The manual gave staff a false sense of security." This means the feeling of safety was…
items.why: False sense = falsa sensação: sentir-se seguro sem estar de fato protegido.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "We rewrote the rules in ___ so a non-technical employee can read them in five minutes."
items.why: Plain language = linguagem simples: clara e acessível para qualquer colaborador.

items.q: "Half the staff could not recognise a phishing email." To recognise here means to…
options: identify or tell what it is
items.why: To recognise = reconhecer: identificar o que a mensagem realmente é.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre segurança e políticas internas. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Legal still has to sign off on the new policy before we launch it." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the refresh to every team over the next quarter." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, equipe por equipe.

items.q: "A few managers pushed back on the rising incident numbers." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, questionar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The team promised to report incidents but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it out to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "A long annual training would not move the needle on real awareness." This means it would…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
